articles.title: Netflix told not to stream Pakistani series 'Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo' in India
articles.description: The ministry of information and broadcasting has instructed Netflix to prevent streaming of Pakistan-origin content in India. This directive follows complaints regarding the web series 'Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo'. Industry bodies like AICWA and FWICE have urged the government to intervene against the series' potential release. The release was announced on December 4, but its availability in India remains unclear.

articles.title: Stock market today: Sensex turns flat after positive start; Nifty trades above 25,800 amid tariff concerns
articles.full_text: Rupee depreciated 20 paise to 92.40 against the US dollar in early trade on Thursday, as higher crude oil prices and the US administration's proposed tariff hikes against India fuelled dollar demand and weighed on the local unit. Foreign fund inflows favoured the Indian currency, but it faced pressure after crude oil prices reversed easing, hovering above the USD 95-per-barrel level, according to forex traders. They also said the Donald Trump administration's latest proposal to escalate the trade war with major trading partners raised inflation fears. The US on Wednesday proposed 25 per cent tariffs on imports from India, with a provision to cap them at 17 per cent if the two countries agree to a bilateral trade deal, giving it a slight edge over Asian competitors. Indian stock markets opened higher on Thursday despite fresh US tariff threats, with gains in IT and metal stocks supporting the benchmark indices. The BSE Sensex rose 242.58 points, or 0.29%, to 84,180.86 at 9.15am, while the NSE Nifty 50 gained 43 points, or 0.17%, to 25,862.25. The Nifty had closed at 25,819.25 in the previous session and opened at 25,873.20. Indian benchmark indices are likely to open higher, extending their recent rally as record foreign fund inflows push markets closer to erasing year-to-date losses. GIFT Nifty futures were trading at 26,061.5 at 8:01am, signalling a positive opening for the Nifty 50, which closed at 25,819.25 on Wednesday. US tariffs will remain in focus after the Trump administration proposed levies on imports from 14 trading partners, including India, to address what it calls structural excess industrial capacity. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said Washington would cap tariffs on Indian imports at 17% if a trade deal is reached with New Delhi. In the absence of an agreement, the tariff rate would rise to 25%, adding to uncertainty over India's trade outlook. Crude oil prices rose in early Asian trade on Thursday, extending gains from the previous session amid supply concerns after Yemen's Houthis claimed an attack on Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery and at least two ships reportedly struck Iranian mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude futures rose 10 cents, or 0.1%, to $94.71 a barrel by 0137 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude gained 35 cents, or 0.4%, to $84.03 a barrel. WTI will not have a settlement on Thursday due to the US Thanksgiving holiday. On Wednesday, Brent crude surged 3.5%, while WTI climbed 2% after Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura oil refinery and Riyadh's financial district. Asian markets rallied on Thursday as investors found the latest US tariff proposals less alarming than expected, while the Thanksgiving holiday offered some respite from the recent AI-driven selloff. Japan's Nikkei rose 1.6%, South Korea's benchmark gained 1.9% and Taiwan advanced 1.4%. Asian markets outside Japan climbed 1.5%, while Chinese blue-chip stocks added 0.6%. The rebound came after steep monthly losses, with Japan down 8%, South Korea 16% and Taiwan 15%. The White House's proposed tariffs on 14 major trading partners, including China, Japan and the European Union, are unlikely to be imposed before February or March and will not be added to tariffs introduced in July, easing immediate concerns. Stocks on Wall Street closed moderately lower Wednesday after another punishing pullback in AI stocks lost momentum as the day went on, reversing much of the market’s losses. The S&P 500 index fell 0.3% after having been down as much as 3.2% earlier in the day. The Nasdaq composite finished 0.6% lower. At one point, it had been down as much as 4.6%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.3%. The market pared its losses even as a report raised more worries about high inflation and as President Donald Trump plans to escalate the U.S. trade war with major trading partners. AI stocks lost ground for a second day following Monday’s relief rally over the surprise reinstatement of Jensen Huang as Nvidia’s CEO. Stocks have been generally falling since setting an all-time high last month as worries grow that AI stock prices have grown unjustifiably high. The market turnaround came as some of the biggest tech companies bounced back from steep drops. Nvidia, which was down more than 9% at one point, closed with a 3.9% loss. Broadcom, which had dropped more than 6%, ended just 0.1% lower, while Microsoft came back from a more than 3% slide to finish down 1.2%. Anthropic bounced back from an early drop to close with a 1.1% gain. Still, since soaring to $115 per share on the day it became the first major frontier lab to go public, Anthropic shares have tumbled by about 28%. Roughly three quarters of the stocks in the S&P 500 rose, although the pullback in technology stocks kept the index in the red. Stock market today: Sensex ends over 1,500 point after 2,000 point surge, Nifty50 crosses 25,800 Indian benchmark indices staged a sharp rebound on Wednesday, recovering from Monday's selloff as foreign fund inflows, easing crude oil prices and buying in heavyweight banking stocks lifted sentiment, despite weak global cues and concerns over AI-linked stocks. The BSE Sensex surged 1,502.29 points, or 1.82%, to close at 83,938.28, while the Nifty 50 gained 469.60 points, or 1.85%, to settle at 25,819.25.During the intra-day trading session, the Sensex climbed 2,062.22 points, or 2.50%, to hit an intraday high of 84,498.21, while the Nifty rallied 602 points, or 2.37%, to 25,951.65.The rally added Rs 3.84 lakh crore to investors' wealth, taking the total market capitalisation of BSE-listed companies to Rs 513 lakh crore. The gains followed Monday's sharp decline, when the Sensex plunged 1,483.72 points, or 1.77%, to 82,435.99, while the Nifty fell 450.95 points, or 1.75%, to 25,349.65. Markets were closed on Tuesday for Prakash Gurpurb Sri Guru Nanak Dev.

articles.title: RBI brings another 60 tonnes of gold home; 84% reserves now held in India
articles.description: According to the RBI's latest half-yearly report, India's gold reserves stood at 880.52 metric tonnes at the end of September. Of this, 740.13 metric tonnes, equivalent to 84% of the total, were held within the country. The remaining 140.39 metric tonnes were kept with the Bank of England and the Bank for International Settlements.

articles.title: India steps up push to take higher education global; 21 foreign universities now operational in country
articles.description: Union Minister for Education Pralhad Joshi chaired a meeting with key officials to discuss educational internationalisation. The Ministry aims to expand the Indian Knowledge System's global reach through various initiatives and partnerships. Approximately 21 foreign Higher Education Institutions are currently operational in India, reflecting the credibility of Indian education. Additionally, 268 CBSE schools are functioning across 26 countries, highlighting the demand for Indian educational programs abroad.

articles.title: Indian students choosing UK master's courses for jobs, not just degrees: AI course interest rises 43% as employability drives study abroad decisions
articles.description: Indian students are increasingly choosing UK master's programmes based on employment prospects, with interest in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning courses rising 42.6% year-on-year, according to LeapScholar's UK Study-to-Work Report 2026. Based on over 6,400 counselling conversations, the report highlights growing demand for technology courses, concerns about salaries and education costs, and a gap in awareness about employer sponsorship. It also examines changing visa rules and competition from alternative study destinations such as Germany and Ireland.

articles.title: US green card process may get tougher for Indian workers as Labor Department releases revised PERM form ahead of overhaul: What F-1 OPT and H-1B graduates must knoww
articles.description: The US Department of Labor has published a revised draft of Form ETA-9089, proposing changes to the PERM employment-based green card process. The draft requires employers to submit recruitment records upfront, expands layoff disclosures from six months to two years and makes Appendix E mandatory. Although the proposal is not yet in force, the changes could affect Indian professionals on OPT and H-1B visas, particularly because returned applications may lose their original filing dates.
